claim: Effective stress is total stress minus pore pressure (Terzaghi, no Biot coefficient).
quote: Effective stress (s' or S') - portion of the applied stress carried by the rock grains; this is estimated as the difference between the total applied stress and pore pressure.

claim: Overburden (vertical stress) is the total load of the water column and sediments, from bulk density.
quote: Overburden (or lithostatic or vertical stress) (SV) - is the total vertical load of the static column of formation water and the overlying sediments, calculated from bulk density.

claim: Effective stress ratio = (Shmin - P) / (Sv - P), the form of the engine's constant K.
quote: Effective stress ratio - empirical ratio of the horizontal to vertical effective stress (Shmin - P)/(Sv - P).

claim: Disequilibrium compaction is the common overpressure mechanism in most basins.
quote: Undercompaction is the common mechanism which generates overpressure in most basin settings.

claim: Fracture pressure is defined by observed losses, with LOP, FBP, FPP, ISIP, FCP and FRP distinguished; FCP is the best approximation to minimum stress.
quote: Fracture Closure Pressure (FCP) - pressure at which the initiated fracture is mechanically closed again, generally the best approximation of the minimum in situ stress.

claim: A FIT does not give minimum stress.
quote: A FIT does not provide minimum principal stress information.

claim: In salt and anhydrite the fracture gradient is at or above the vertical stress; a 500-800 psi tensile term is often added.
quote: In salt and anhydrite layers, the fracture gradient is generally equal to or above vertical stress. A tensile strength of 500-800 psi is often considered in the computation of fracture gradient in evaporites.

claim: Fracture gradient is calibrated to LOP; where poorly calibrated, use the lower end of the range.
quote: In general, the fracture gradient is calibrated to the leak-off pressure (LOP).

claim: Basin models suit burial-related (disequilibrium compaction) overpressure and scenario testing.
quote: Basin models are more likely to accurately represent systems dominated by burial-related overpressure (disequilibrium compaction or primary overpressure).

claim: A pre-drill PPFG forecast generally contains overburden, pore pressure, fracture pressure and/or minimum stress, and their uncertainties.
quote: A pre-drill PPFG forecast generally contains the following curves:

claim: Vertical stress is the integral of the density profile from sea level or ground level.
quote: Vertical stress is calculated by integrating the density profile from sea level/ground level to planned well TD, which requires a continuous density curve with depth.

claim: A single-point pore pressure prediction is not sufficient; a range is required.
quote: A single-point pore pressure prediction for a reservoir is not considered sufficient. It can be misleading and even hazardous.

claim: Evaporites are impermeable and pore pressure is not relevant inside them; enclosed inclusions can reach 85-95 percent of vertical stress.
quote: Evaporites are generally impermeable; pore pressure is not relevant because there is not usually any fluid filled pore space in evaporite sequences.

claim: Inclusions or rafts inside salt may carry pressures of about 85-95 percent of vertical stress (empirical, no source given).
quote: Depending on the geological environment, empirical observations indicate it can be as high as approximately 85% to 95% of vertical stress.

claim: Rock does not uncompact when effective stress falls; unloading leaves high density with low velocity and undercompaction methods underpredict.
quote: If overpressures are generated after compaction, then rock properties depart from their compaction trends because the rocks cannot "uncompact" as vertical effective stress (VES) decreases during overpressure generation.

claim: A velocity reversal is the signal to consider unloading.
quote: While they may or may not occur with depth for undercompaction, unloading will create a velocity reversal. Therefore, whenever a velocity reversal is observed, unloading mechanisms should be considered.

claim: Salt tectonics and allochthonous bodies redistribute stress and change initial pressure in surrounding rock.
quote: Salt tectonics, diapirism and allochthones rock bodies presence can lead a stress redistribution and changes in initial pressure of surrounding rocks.

claim: Minimum horizontal stress comes from a 1D-strain poro-elasto-plastic model with an effective stress ratio, or a fault-stability model; it is calibrated to closure pressure.
quote: Minimum horizontal stress is generally, calibrated to the fracture closure pressure interpreted from pressure integrity tests (LOT, XLOT, minifrac).

claim: Horizontal stress is generally higher in shale than in sand or limestone.
quote: Horizontal stress is generally greater in shale than in sandstone and/or limestone.

claim: Fracture pressure rarely equals far-field minimum stress.
quote: Fracture pressure rarely equals the far-field minimum stress.

claim: The most likely (P50) case is used for primary design; low and high cases for contingency.
quote: The most likely pore and fracture pressure estimate is used for primary well design, while contingency scenarios should cover the low and high estimate scenarios.

claim: Sample plots show a fracture range from Shmin to formation breakdown with an estimated gradient from average effective stress ratios between them.
quote: Figure also includes fracture pressure gradient (and ranges; from the minimum horizontal stress to formation breakdown pressure, with an estimated fracture gradient based on average effective stress ratios in between).

claim: Sample plot Figure 7: fracture range from Shmin to formation breakdown, estimated minimum fracture gradient, offset pressure integrity tests posted, ranges from the most likely pore pressure; axes in sg against TVD RT.
quote: In this case the ranges are from the minimum horizontal stress to formation breakdown pressure, with an estimated minimum fracture gradient and various pressure integrity tests from offset wells. These ranges are estimated from the most likely pore pressure.

claim: The report does not cover wellbore stability.
quote: The document does not cover any activity related to wellbore stability.
